heading: Application for Analyst Graduate Programme 26/27
paragraphs: I am applying for the Analyst Graduate Programme, with a preference for the Identity Access and Management practice. The work described there, access provisioning and deprovisioning, joiner-mover-leaver processes, authentication and authorisation, is what I already handle day to day in a smaller setting, and I want to build on it properly under experienced consultants. I am available to start in November 2026.

My background combines formal security training with hands-on access administration. I hold an MSc in Information Security from Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, and a BCA in computer applications, along with CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity. My MSc covered security management, critical infrastructure security and secure business architectures, which gave me a grounding in the governance side of identity work rather than only the tooling.

The clearest match to your IAM practice is my current role. I manage four to five access requests a day through on-premises Active Directory, verifying business approval before granting time-limited permissions, documenting access periods and extensions, and maintaining a clear audit trail. I handle account creation, permission changes and deprovisioning, which is the joiner-mover-leaver process in practice. I also support user access reviews and raise access-related risks when I see them, such as permissions that outlast their business need. At Co-op I conduct weekly risk assessments and daily compliance checks, maintaining records and following up until identified risks are addressed, which is the control discipline your Risk, Security and Controls practice describes.

On the eligibility criteria, I should be straightforward. I hold an honours degree and permanent right to work in the UK. My school qualifications are Indian CBSE Class XII rather than A-levels, with strong results in English and Computer Science. I also do not have commercial experience with SailPoint, CyberArk or SAP, which your advert mentions, though I have the Active Directory and access governance foundations those tools build on.

What attracts me to Turnkey is the consulting model. Working across client environments rather than inside one organisation would expose me to a range of governance and control problems, and the structured progression through CISMP to a specialist certification matches how I want to develop. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my access management experience could contribute to your team. Thank you for considering my application.
